direction: Narrow to a single, hop-depth-conditional, matched-budget training-time experiment that separates the reasoning chain from peripheral same-passage context, and evaluate it under matched inference-time context against a training-free context baseline. Drop the repair loop and RL stage from the primary contribution (or demote them to clearly labeled secondary experiments), and treat the outcome as a pre-registered boundary/negative result about when context supervision helps rather than as a new state-of-the-art method.
hypothesis: H1': Under a matched supervision token budget and identical inference-time context, supervision that exposes the full reasoning chain improves multi-hop (>=2-hop) KGQA over isolated-triple supervision, while adding peripheral same-passage triples beyond the chain yields no measurable improvement (and a matched-budget shuffled-triple arm performs no better than peripheral same-passage triples). H2': Any advantage of context-enriched training disappears when test-time context is held constant across arms. H3': Per-hop failure attribution (one-hop failure rate) and a hop-depth transfer gap can be measured reliably and characterize where errors originate.
rationale: The evidence supports neither the original bundled scope nor rejecting the direction. The premise is challenged (non-chain context triples contribute only +0.003 F1 at inference; over-retrieval introduces distractors), the mechanism is largely prior art (path supervision, text graphs, self-bootstrapping), and H2 is unsupported - so continuing as proposed would be uninterpretable. But one unoccupied and inexpensive question survives: no retrieved work tests context-enriched supervision versus triple-only supervision under a matched budget and matched inference context, and the hop-depth-conditional prediction gives a falsifiable form that distinguishes chain effects from peripheral-context effects. This deserves investigation next because it is cheap, decisive for the original premise, and yields a useful boundary result either way. It is not claimed to be the best possible direction for the field, only the most informative next step for this idea.
research_question: Under a matched supervision token budget and identical inference-time context, does training-time exposure to the full reasoning chain (and, separately, to peripheral same-passage context triples) change multi-hop KGQA accuracy by hop depth relative to isolated-triple supervision, and does any gain survive controlling for test-time context and token budget?
